title: Customer acquisition cost (CAC)
reading_md:
**What it measures.** What it costs, on average, to win one new customer. A new customer is someone placing a first order ever. A returning customer is not new, however much was spent on reaching them again.

**Formula.** CAC = cost / new customers. Grain: channel or company × period. There are two versions, so always say which one you mean.

| Version | Cost | Customers |
|---|---|---|
| Blended CAC | All sales and marketing cost: media, agencies, the marketing team | All new customers, from every channel, paid or not |
| Paid CAC (per channel) | That channel's paid media spend | New customers attributed to that channel |

Use paid CAC per channel to decide where the next euro of budget goes. Blended CAC describes the company as a whole.

**Worked example.** In one quarter Voltmarkt's total sales and marketing cost was €750,000, and 25,000 customers placed their first order.

- Blended CAC = 750,000 / 25,000 = €30.00.

Paid search cost €180,000 and was credited with 4,000 first orders from new customers, plus 2,000 orders from returning customers.

- Paid search CAC = 180,000 / 4,000 = €45.00.
- Dividing by all 6,000 orders gives €30.00. That is a cost per order, not CAC.

The blended €30 looks cheaper than paid search's €45 because the blended count includes customers who arrived through organic search, word of mouth or a store visit at no media cost. That is why blended CAC must not drive a channel budget decision.

**Common mistakes.**

- Quoting blended CAC when deciding channel budgets.
- Counting returning customers as new. CAC then looks lower than it is.
- Changing what the cost includes, such as media only in one quarter and media plus agency fees in the next. Label what the cost covers.

**What CAC does not answer.**

- Whether the customers are worth what they cost. That needs their margin and repeat orders over time (in SaaS, LTV and CAC payback).
- How much revenue the spend brought back: that is ROAS.
- What a click or a single order costs: those are CPC and CPA.

**How managers ask for it.** "What does it cost us to get a new customer?" "Is paid search CAC going up?"
